summary: Configured node1 to rotate /var/log/inventory/app.log daily, retain seven compressed rotations, and use copytruncate so open writers continue writing. The configuration, scheduler, logs, and archives persisted across a verified node restart.
actions_performed: Installed logrotate and its OpenRC integration.
Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory with daily, rotate 7, compress, and copytruncate.
Enabled and started crond; confirmed the daily logrotate job is executable.
Tested rotation with an open writer and verified writing continued afterward.
Verified exactly seven valid gzip archives are retained.
Restarted node1 safely and verified its boot identity changed and logging services/data recovered.

evidence.summary: crond is enabled and running, the daily logrotate job is executable, and the parsed inventory policy reports a one-day interval.
Forced retention testing produced exactly app.log.1.gz through app.log.7.gz; all archives passed gzip validation and remained present after restart.

evidence.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation
evidence.summary: A process held app.log open across rotation. The inode stayed unchanged, pre-rotation data entered the compressed archive, and the same writer successfully appended to the active log afterward.

Captured healthy baseline boot ID 157cfd8f-a9b2-41c0-8275-02e84c450ecf, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID 8d610cb7-0ca5-4236-a553-92f3daf61558, and post-restart proof of active/enabled crond, executable daily job, persisted policy/data, and seven healthy archives.
